pages.quiz:
SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY — TERMLY EXAM #2 (TERM 2)
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY
TIME ALLOWED: 60 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 50
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Which of these can be poured and takes the shape of its container? (1 mark)
   A. Book
   B. Water
   C. Brick
   D. Stone

2. Steam from a boiling pot is really (1 mark)
   A. A white solid
   B. An invisible gas
   C. A block of ice
   D. A red liquid

3. Why are liquids useful for drinking? (1 mark)
   A. They can be poured and swallowed
   B. They keep their own shape
   C. They cannot flow
   D. They are always hot

4. What happens to a liquid when you pour it into a different container? (1 mark)
   A. It disappears
   B. It keeps its old shape
   C. It becomes a solid
   D. It takes the shape of the new container

5. Which of these is matter? (1 mark)
   A. Water
   B. Sound
   C. Heat
   D. Light

6. Which unit is used for the mass of a sack of maize? (1 mark)
   A. Kilogram
   B. Second
   C. Litre
   D. Metre

7. A bag has 1 kg of rice and 250 g of beans. What is the total mass? (1 mark)
   A. 1250 g
   B. 2500 g
   C. 350 g
   D. 1025 g

8. Sand pours like a liquid. What state is each grain? (1 mark)
   A. Solid
   B. Liquid
   C. Steam
   D. Gas

9. Which waste goes into a compost pit? (1 mark)
   A. Vegetable peelings
   B. Plastic bags
   C. Tins
   D. Glass

10. What is solid waste? (1 mark)
   A. Air from a tyre
   B. Unwanted solid material that is thrown away
   C. Dirty water
   D. Smoke from a fire

11. What is the danger of leaving plastic bags on the ground? (1 mark)
   A. They grow into plants
   B. They turn into soil fast
   C. They make the soil rich
   D. They stay for a long time and block drains

12. Which disease can spread by mosquitoes breeding in old tins that hold water? (1 mark)
   A. Toothache
   B. Sunburn
   C. Diarrhoea only
   D. Malaria

13. What should you wear when collecting waste? (1 mark)
   A. A hat only
   B. Gloves and closed shoes
   C. Sandals only
   D. Nothing

14. What does the word biodegradable mean? (1 mark)
   A. Able to be broken down by living things
   B. Made of glass
   C. Made of plastic
   D. Not able to rot

15. Which item can be reused as a toy wheel? (1 mark)
   A. Leaves
   B. Banana peel
   C. Ash
   D. Bottle tops

16. When is the best time to water plants? (1 mark)
   A. Early morning or evening
   B. Noon
   C. Midday only
   D. Never

17. What should be done with stored rainwater before drinking? (1 mark)
   A. Freeze it only
   B. Drink it directly
   C. Add soil
   D. Boil or treat it

18. Which of these is a way of protecting water sources? (1 mark)
   A. Washing clothes in the river
   B. Planting trees near rivers
   C. Letting animals dirty the spring
   D. Throwing waste in the river

19. Why do we need water for farming? (1 mark)
   A. To bake bricks only
   B. Crops and livestock need water
   C. To make stones
   D. To make wind

20. Which reused water is safe for drinking? (1 mark)
   A. Water that washed a car
   B. None of the used washing water
   C. Water that washed vegetables
   D. Water that washed clothes

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
21. Write three ways of managing waste in the classroom. (3 marks)

22. Group these into solid, liquid and gas: milk, chalk, oxygen, cooking oil, book, steam. (4 marks)

23. Explain the dangers of solid waste to health, animals and the environment. (5 marks)

24. List four water-saving habits that pupils can practise at school. (4 marks)

25. Write two uses of each of these: solids, liquids and gases. (Choose any four uses in all.) (4 marks)

26. A family of five uses a tap that drips 1 litre every hour. Calculate how much water is wasted in one week and suggest what they should do. (5 marks)

27. Why is used washing water not safe for drinking? Give one good way to use it. (3 marks)

28. Give two ways of reducing waste at home. (2 marks)
pages.answers:
SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY — TERMLY EXAM #2 (TERM 2) · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. B — Water
   Water is a liquid.

2. B — An invisible gas
   Steam is water as a gas and is invisible. The cloud we see is tiny water drops.

3. A — They can be poured and swallowed
   Liquids pour easily.

4. D — It takes the shape of the new container
   A liquid has no shape of its own.

5. A — Water
   Water has mass and takes up space. Light, sound and heat are not matter.

6. A — Kilogram
   Mass is measured in grams and kilograms.

7. A — 1250 g
   1 kg = 1000 g, and 1000 + 250 = 1250 g.

8. A — Solid
   Each grain is a small solid.

9. A — Vegetable peelings
   Only decomposable waste is composted.

10. B — Unwanted solid material that is thrown away
   Solid waste is unwanted solid material.

11. D — They stay for a long time and block drains
   Plastic bags stay for years and block drains.

12. D — Malaria
   Mosquitoes spread malaria and breed in standing water.

13. B — Gloves and closed shoes
   Gloves and shoes protect from cuts and germs.

14. A — Able to be broken down by living things
   Biodegradable waste rots naturally.

15. D — Bottle tops
   Bottle tops make good wheels for toys.

16. A — Early morning or evening
   Less water evaporates when it is cooler.

17. D — Boil or treat it
   Boiling or treating kills germs.

18. B — Planting trees near rivers
   Tree roots hold the soil and protect water.

19. B — Crops and livestock need water
   Water is needed for plants and animals.

20. B — None of the used washing water
   Used washing water is not safe to drink.

SECTION B
----
21. (3 marks)
   Answer: Use a bin with a lid, put paper in a separate box for reusing, do not litter, make monitors.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

22. (4 marks)
   Answer: Solids: chalk and book. Liquids: milk and cooking oil. Gases: oxygen and steam.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct pair.

23. (5 marks)
   Answer: Health: flies and rats spread diseases, mosquitoes breed in tins. Animals: goats eat polythene and die. Environment: blocked drains, polluted water, harmful smoke from burning.
   Working / marking points: 2 marks for health, 1 mark for animals and 2 marks for environment.

24. (4 marks)
   Answer: Close taps, report leaks, use a bucket for watering the garden, water plants in the morning or evening, use a cup to drink.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

25. (4 marks)
   Answer: Solids: building, tools, clothes. Liquids: drinking, washing, cooking, fuel. Gases: breathing, cooking gas, inflating tyres.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct use up to 4.

26. (5 marks)
   Answer: 24 x 7 = 168 litres. They should repair the tap or ask an adult or plumber to fix it.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for 24 hours, 1 mark for 24 x 7, 1 mark for 168, 1 mark for fixing the tap, 1 mark for units.

27. (3 marks)
   Answer: It has dirt and germs. It can be used to water plants or mop floors.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for dirty water, 1 mark for germs, 1 mark for a safe use.

28. (2 marks)
   Answer: Buy less packaging, carry a reusable bag, cook only what is needed, repair things.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.
